title: Multi-step Preparation Technique to Recover Multiple Metabolite Compound Classes for In-depth and Informative Metabolomic Analysis
protocol: Use glass for storing lipids and organic solvents.
Seal polytetrafluoroethylene caps tightly to avoid air exposure and evaporation.
Resuspend dried lipids in the next solvent immediately or keep them in a steady stream of nitrogen.
Turn on centrifuge and set to 0 °C prior to starting sample preparation.
Keep all solvents capped during sample preparation.
Prepare two types of standards as recommended.
Prepare a negative control with spiked-in standards at constant concentration for all samples.
Use a pooled sample spiked with standards as a batch QC for monitoring reproducibility across separate days.
Utilize previously prepared, sub-aliquoted spiked pooled samples to monitor instrument conditions and fluctuations during analysis.
Prepare positive controls at concentrations of 1x, 2x, and 4x standard spikes.
Store standards at -20°C.
Store samples at -80°C.
Ensure that the chosen ISTD covers a wide range of the chromatogram.
Create hydrophilic stock solutions at 2 mg/ml using isotopically labeled standards and/or other polar compounds exogenous to the sample being analyzed.
Dilute each stock solution in 1:1 methanol:water.
Prepare one solution with all standards to a final concentration of 25 µg/ml creatinine-D3, 100 µg/ml lysine-D4, and 200 µg/ml valine-D8.
Create hydrophobic stock solutions using isotopically labeled standards and non-polar compounds.
Mix 17:0 fatty acid to a concentration of 4 mg/ml.
Mix 19:1 fatty acid to a concentration of 4 mg/ml.
Mix 17:0 ceramide to a concentration of 2 mg/ml.
Mix 17:0 PE to a concentration of 1.75 mg/ml.
Mix 15:0 PC to a concentration of 2 mg/ml.
Mix testosterone-D2 to a concentration of 1 mg/ml.

Create one solution in 1:1 chloroform:methanol with all standards at final concentrations of 50 µg/ml 17:0 ceramide, 100 µg/ml 15:0 PC, 100 µg/ml testosterone-D2, 200 µg/ml 17:0 fatty acid, 200 µg/ml 19:1 fatty acid, and 200 µg/ml 17:0 PE in the standard mix.
Test the degree of ionization of each standard using at least five different concentrations to determine the limit of detection and linearity of the instrument.
Create a spike mix of positive controls.
Add positive controls to samples at 1x, 2x, or 4x concentration levels.
Final concentrations can be: 2 mg/ml D-glucose, 100 µg/ml alanine-D3, 200 µg/ml methylmalonic acid-D3, and 20 µg/ml triglyceride-D5.
Thaw samples to room temperature.
Spike 10 µl of ISTD to each sample.
Add 10 µl of both hydrophilic and hydrophobic standard solutions to each sample.
Adjust standard concentrations based on MS and HPLC sensitivity.
Vortex each sample for 10 seconds prior to the protein precipitation step.
Add 400 µl of ice cold methanol to each sample.
Vortex again for 10 seconds per tube.
Centrifuge at -20 °C for 15 minutes at 18,000 x g.
Transfer all supernatant to a new glass culture tube.
Dry the supernatant under N2.
If analyzing the protein pellet fraction, proceed to steps for MTBE extraction.
Add 1 ml of MTBE to the white (or off-white) protein pellet.
Vortex for 30 sec per tube.
Centrifuge at 0 °C for 15 min at 18,000 x g.
Decant the MTBE layer to a new glass culture tube.
Consistently aspirate the same amount of MTBE for ALL samples since the size of the pellet will vary among samples.
Repeat step of adding 1 ml of MTBE to the protein pellet.
Combine the organic layer with the previous MTBE layer in the same glass culture tube.
Dry samples by N2 flow.
Resuspend dried samples in 200 μl of 1:1 chloroform:methanol.
Vortex briefly.
Transfer resuspended sample to a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 0 °C for 15 min at 18,000 x g.
Transfer supernatant to autosampler screw cap vials using glass pipettes.
Using a glass pipette, add 3 ml of MTBE to the dried methanol residual.
Vortex for 30 seconds.
Add 750 μl of water and vortex for 10 seconds per tube.
Spin at approximately 200 x g for 10 minutes in a centrifuge at room temperature.
Aspirate 2.5 ml of the MTBE layer without getting any water.
Transfer the aspirated MTBE to a clean glass culture tube.
Add 3 ml of MTBE to the remaining water part of the sample and vortex for 10 seconds per tube.
Spin at approximately 200 x g for 10 minutes in the centrifuge at room temperature.
Aspirate 3 ml of the MTBE layer without getting any water.
Combine the aspirated MTBE with the previous MTBE tube.
Concentrate the remaining aqueous layer by drying under nitrogen gas.
Re-suspend the residue in 100 μl of water.
Add 400 μl of ice cold methanol to the glass culture tube and vortex briefly.
Transfer the mixture to a microcentrifuge tube.
Leave at -80 °C for 20-30 minutes.
Spin at 0 °C for 15 minutes at 18,000 x g.
Place the entire sample rack in a -80 °C freezer.
Aspirate 450 μl of supernatant and transfer to a clean microcentrifuge tube.
Dry completely in a vacuum centrifugal concentrator at no more than 45 °C.
Resuspend dried supernatant in 200 μl of 5% acetonitrile/water.
Vortex briefly.
Freeze the resuspended supernatant at -80 °C.
Dry the MTBE fraction under nitrogen at 35 °C with a good flow of nitrogen.
Stop the flow of nitrogen and quickly resuspend in 1 ml chloroform using a glass pipette.
Vortex briefly.
Warm samples to room temperature and keep suspended under a steady flow of N2.
Wash and condition SPE cartridge twice with 400 µl hexane, discard waste and replace with new glass collection tube.
Add sample to SPE column, collect flow through in glass tubes.
With glass pipette add 1 ml of 2:1 CHCl3:IPA, collect flow through in same glass tubes (this is the Neutral Fraction).
Dry the neutral fraction under N2 to minimize oxidation.
With glass pipette add 1 ml of 5% acetic acid in diethyl ether, collect flow through in new glass tubes (this is the Fatty Acid Fraction).
Dry the fatty acid fraction under N2 to minimize oxidation.
Use plastic tips to add 800 µl of methanol to SPE cartridge, and collect flow-through in 15 ml plastic conical tubes (this is the Phospholipid Fraction).
Transfer phospholipid fraction to 1.5 ml centrifuge tubes.
Dry the samples with a vacuum centrifugal concentrator at 45 °C.
Resuspend each of the samples from the three fractions in 200 µl of 100% methanol, vortex, and transfer to autosampler vials screw-cap for storage.
Store all samples at -80°C until ready for instrument analysis.
Use a C-18 2.1 mm x 50 mm (1.8 μm) analytical column with a C-18 2.1 mm x 12.5 mm (5 μm) guard column for liquid chromatography analysis of the hydrophobic fraction.
Set the autosampler temperature to 4 °C.
Set the column temperature to 60 °C.
Inject 2 µl sample volume.
Maintain a flow rate of 0.25 ml/min.
Use 0.1% formic acid in water as mobile phase A.
Use 0.1% formic acid in isopropanol:acetonitrile:water (60:36:4) as mobile phase B.
Start at 30% B, increase to 70% B from 0 to 1 min.
Increase to 100% B from 1 to 15 min and hold for 5 min.
Wash with 10% B for 5 min.
Post-run analysis follows a 5 min wash period.
Set the autosampler temperature to 4 °C.
Set the column temperature to 20 °C.
Set the injection volume to 2 µl.
Set the flow rate to 0.5 ml/min.
Use 50% acetonitrile in 10 mM ammonium acetate, pH 5.8 for mobile phase A.
Use 90% acetonitrile in 10 mM ammonium acetate, pH 5.8 for mobile phase B.
Start at 100% B from 0 to 2 min.
Decrease to 50% B from 2 to 15 min.
Wash with 0% B for 5 min.
Run post run for 10 min.
